title: How to organise the hanging and air-dry zone | Laundry Room
description:
Dry the few things a hot drum would ruin, and get them off the rack the moment they are dry.

This is the Hanging and Air-Dry Zone in the Laundry Room. About 15-30 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
The rack folded flat against the wall with dry bars, its drip tray wiped out and empty, the rail holding six spare hangers, and nothing hanging that was washed before today.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Strip the rack completely.
Straighten: The rack gets one spot with a drip tray underneath, not wherever the last load abandoned it.
Shine: A rack that is stored damp grows a musty smell and passes it straight to the next load hung on it.
Safety: Water on a hard floor under a drying rack is a slip you take in socks with an armful of laundry.
Standardize: The rack is either in use holding one set of damp items, or folded flat against the wall.
Sustain: Before you open the washer to start the next load, you clear the rack.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
The rack is in use or folded flat, never left standing half loaded.

Full written steps for this zone, free:
https://6s-success.com/zones/laundry-room-the-hanging-and-air-dry-zone.html

6S Success turns Lean's six-S method into something you can actually do in a house: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain. One small zone at a time, finished in one session, and it stays finished.
